app.name: Twalk Companion
app.tagline: The command center for your sovereign messaging hub
screen1.description: Twalk brings all your conversations — WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Google Messages — into one place you own, watched over by agents you configure. This Companion sets everything up for you.
screen1.domain.label: Your Twalk domain
screen1.domain.invalid: Please enter a valid domain like {example}.
onboarding.title: Create your account
onboarding.domain: Twalk will set up your account on {domain}.
onboarding.pending.title: This step is on its way
onboarding.pending.body: Account creation and your recovery key arrive with the bootstrap journey. The foundation this screen sits on — the app shell, the Gateway client, the capability check — is in place.
gate.title: This browser cannot run Twalk yet
gate.intro: {count, plural, one {One thing this browser needs is missing.} other {# things this browser needs are missing.}} Twalk does its cryptography here, in the page, so your recovery key never leaves your device — and that needs all of them.
gate.degraded.intro: Everything onboarding needs is here. These extras are not, so some conveniences will be missing.
gate.cause.insecure-context: The page was not loaded over a secure connection. Browsers switch off the cryptography, storage and installation Twalk needs outside HTTPS. Open the Companion over {https}, or over {localhost} while developing.
gate.cause.lockdown-mode: This looks like iOS Lockdown Mode: WebAssembly still runs, but local storage, installation and tab locking are switched off. Open Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Lockdown Mode, and allow this site — or open Twalk in another browser.
gate.cause.storage-blocked: Local storage is switched off. A private window, or a browser setting that blocks site data, does this. Open the Companion in a normal window and allow site data for {origin}.
gate.cause.unsupported-browser: This browser is missing something Twalk needs. Twalk supports Safari on iOS 16.4 and later, and current versions of Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
gate.capability.secure-context.why: HTTPS, or localhost. Everything below depends on it.
gate.capability.webassembly.why: Runs the Matrix cryptography that generates your keys.
gate.capability.storage.why: Keeps your keys on this device, and nowhere else.
gate.capability.crypto-subtle.why: Generates the randomness your recovery key is made of.
gate.capability.service-worker.why: Lets you install Twalk to your home screen.
gate.capability.tab-lock.why: Stops two open tabs from corrupting your keys.
gate.checking: Checking what this browser can do…
version.mismatch.title: Twalk has been updated
version.mismatch.body: This page was built for Twalk {expected}, and your server now runs {actual}. Reloading to pick up the new version.
version.staleShell.title: A newer Twalk Companion is ready
version.staleShell.body: Your server now serves build {shipped}, and this page is still running build {running}. Reload to pick it up — until then, what you see may not be what was fixed.
version.unreachable: Your Twalk server could not be reached, so its version is unknown. The app still works; some screens will not.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Which model reads your conversations, and which language your assistant falls back to. Each control says what leaves this machine when you use it.
settings.refused.notConfigured: This deployment keeps no settings: its Gateway has no store for them, so nothing here can be saved. Your administrator sets the model in the deployment's configuration instead.
settings.refused.storeUnavailable: The settings store could not be read or written. Nothing changed; try again, and if it persists, your administrator will find the reason in the Gateway's log.
settings.model.title: The model
settings.model.intro: Twalk ships no model and has no default: until one is named here, an assistant refuses to start. What you name is where your contacts' messages are sent to be read — every message an active assistant handles leaves this machine for that endpoint. An OpenAI-compatible proxy on this host is the shape the reference deployment uses.
settings.model.unset: No model is configured. An activated assistant produces nothing until one is.
settings.model.baseUrl.label: Endpoint
settings.model.baseUrl.help: The chat-completions base URL, not the completions path: http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1, not …/chat/completions. An address on this host's loopback is reachable from the assistant's containers on the reference deployment.
settings.model.baseUrl.notAUrl: This is not an http or https address with a host.
settings.model.name.label: Model
settings.model.name.help: The model's name at that endpoint — what your proxy calls it. There is no default.
settings.model.credential.label: Credential
settings.model.credential.help: The key the endpoint expects, if it expects one. It is stored on your server and never shown again here — only that one is set, and its last characters.
settings.model.credential.set: A credential is set, ending in {hint}. It is never shown again here.
settings.model.credential.keep: Leave this empty to keep the credential that is set; type a new one to replace it.
settings.model.credential.file: The credential comes from a file on the server ({path}), which your administrator placed there. It wins over anything set here, so there is nothing to type.
settings.model.credential.fileOverrides: A credential set from this screen earlier exists too, and is ignored while the file is in force.
settings.model.params.label: Provider parameters (JSON object)
settings.model.params.help: Merged into every request untouched — a parameter set to null removes a field the request would otherwise carry. The escape hatch for an endpoint with no proxy in front: a parameter the provider rejects only shows up at the first model call, not here.
settings.model.params.notAnObject: This has to be a JSON object, like '{'"temperature": 0.2'}'.
settings.model.probe.cost: Testing sends one real one-token completion — the word “ping” — to the endpoint. It is the only thing in Twalk that costs you a model call without a message arriving first; no message content is sent.
settings.model.saved: Saved. The runtime reads this at its next start: an assistant already running keeps the model it started with until it is restarted.
settings.model.forgotten: Forgotten, and the credential set from this screen with it. No assistant can start until a model is named again.
settings.model.refused.invalidBaseUrl: The endpoint is not an absolute http or https address with a host. It is the chat-completions base (http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1), not the completions path.
settings.model.refused.invalidModel: The model name is empty, and there is no default.
settings.model.refused.invalidParams: The provider parameters are not a JSON object.
settings.model.refused.invalidCredential: The credential is not a string. An empty one is refused: use “Forget the model” to remove it.
settings.model.refused.malformed: Your server did not recognise what this page sent — a member missing or unknown. That is a defect in the Companion rather than in what you typed; reload the page, and report it if it persists.
settings.probe.notConfigured: There is nothing to test yet: name a model first.
settings.probe.unreachable: Nothing answered at the endpoint — DNS, the connection, TLS, or ten seconds passed. The usual cause on a real deployment is an address your server can reach and an assistant's container cannot; check the address and where it is reachable from.
settings.probe.refused: The endpoint answered and said no ({status}). A 401 or 403 is the credential; a 404 or 400 is usually the model name.
settings.probe.notCompatible: The endpoint answered, but not with a chat completion. That is almost always the wrong port or path — the base URL should end where /chat/completions begins.
settings.probe.ok: The endpoint answered ({status}) as model “{model}”. That is the name it will answer your assistant as: check it is the model you meant, not only that something answered.
settings.language.title: Your language
settings.language.effect: Two things follow from this choice, and only these two: this interface speaks it, and it is the language your assistant writes in when it cannot tell what language a message was written in.
settings.language.notTheReply: It does not decide the language a suggested reply is written in: a reply follows the conversation, so an English-speaking contact is answered in English whatever is chosen here.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.none: No preference — an ambiguous message is answered in whatever language the model picks
settings.language.saved: Saved. The runtime reads this at its next start; this page speaks it now.
settings.language.refused.unsupported: That language is not one of the five the Companion ships.
settings.tracing.title: Tracing
settings.tracing.pending: Tracing what your assistant reasoned — the prompt it was sent, the answer, how long it took — is decided (it will be OpenTelemetry, off until an endpoint is set, with the messages' content behind a second switch of its own) and not yet something this deployment can store. When it is, the controls will be here, and the content switch will say plainly that your contacts' messages then leave for the tracing backend.
settings.tracing.contentWarning: Until then nothing is traced, and nothing leaves this machine for it.
diagnostics.intro: Twalk collects no telemetry and sends nothing to a third party. Nothing on this page leaves your device unless you copy it and send it yourself.
diagnostics.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the text below and copy it by hand.

networks.skip: Skip for now, I'll add networks later
networks.footer: You can add or remove networks at any time from the dashboard.
networks.loading: Reading what this deployment can connect…
networks.unknownList: The networks it can connect are therefore unknown; the cards below are the ones Twalk supports.

networks.card.notConfigured: No bridge for this network is configured on your Twalk server.
networks.bridgesUnreadable.title: This screen could not start
networks.noBridge.title: This network is not configured
networks.noBridge.body: Your Twalk server has no bridge for {network}. Turn on the bridges profile of your deployment, then come back to this screen.
networks.expiresIn: This code refreshes in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.
networks.expired: This code expired before it was scanned.
networks.conflict.title: A login is already in progress
networks.conflict.body: Another of your devices, {device}, started a login at {started} and it is still running. Only one login at a time is possible on a network.
networks.conflict.takeOver: Take it over on this device
networks.trouble.unauthenticated: Your session on this Twalk server has expired. Sign in again to continue.
networks.trouble.tooManyLogins: The network refuses another linked device on this account. Remove one on the network itself, then try again.
networks.trouble.bridge: Your Twalk server could not reach the bridge for this network. Check that it is running, then try again.
networks.trouble.bridgeAnswerUnusable: The bridge for this network is running and answered your Twalk server — Twalk could not make sense of the answer. Nothing is wrong with your server, your bridge or your connection, so there is nothing for you to fix: this is a defect in Twalk. Please report it, and include what your Twalk server logged.
networks.trouble.network: The connection to your Twalk server dropped. Retrying…
networks.trouble.unexpected: Something went wrong on your Twalk server. Try again, and open the diagnostics if it persists.
networks.trouble.refused: Your Twalk server answered and would not accept that request. Nothing is wrong with your server or your connection: this is a defect in Twalk. Please report it, and include what your Twalk server logged.
networks.failed.loginLost: The login was lost: your Twalk server or its bridge restarted while it was running. Nothing about a login in progress survives a restart. Start again.
networks.failed.expired: The network ended this login: the code timed out, or it was already used. Start again.
networks.failed.webauthn: The network asked for a passkey, which the Companion cannot present. Finish this login in the network's own app, or connect this network from another device.
networks.failed.unsupportedStep: The network asked for a step Twalk does not know how to run. Nothing was connected.
networks.failed.bridge: The bridge refused this login. Check that it is running and correctly configured, then try again.
networks.qrAlt: A code to scan with the network’s own app.
networks.cookies.wanted: {count, plural, one {The cookie your bridge asked for} other {The # cookies your bridge asked for}}:
networks.cookies.domain: Your bridge says they belong to {domain}.
networks.cookies.label: Paste the cookies here
networks.cookies.unreadable: That could not be read as cookies. Paste either “name=value; name=value”, or the JSON your cookie extension exports.
networks.cookies.missing: These are missing: {names}. Your browser did not include them in what you copied — the Application › Storage › Cookies view lists every cookie of the site, so copy from there rather than from a request.
networks.jar.wanted: {count, plural, one {The value your bridge asked for} other {The # values your bridge asked for}}, as your browser sends them:
networks.jar.label: Paste them here as JSON
networks.field.empty: Fill this in before sending it.
networks.field.pattern: That is not the shape this network accepts for this field. Check it before sending: a value the network refuses ends the login, and you would have to start again.
networks.field.blockedTitle: This step cannot be answered here
networks.field.blockedBody: Sending part of it would not get you a correction: the network ends the login when it refuses an answer, and you would have to start over anyway. Update Twalk if an update is available, or finish this login in the network’s own app.
networks.field.refusedNoType: Twalk will not draw “{field}”: your bridge did not say what kind of value it is, and guessing could put a password on screen in plain text.
networks.field.refusedUnknownType: Twalk will not draw “{field}”: this version does not know the field type “{type}”, and guessing could put a password on screen in plain text.
networks.field.refusedNoOptions: Twalk will not draw “{field}”: your bridge asked for a choice and listed nothing to choose from, and picking for you is worse than saying so.
networks.field.leftOut: “{field}” is not being sent: this version cannot collect it, and your bridge says the login does not need it.
networks.step.submit: Send this to my Twalk server
networks.step.neverStored: Nothing on this screen is saved in your browser. Close the tab and what you typed is gone.
networks.step.driftTitle: Twalk’s own instructions no longer match this question
networks.step.driftBody: Twalk has its own explanation for this step, written for {expected}, and your bridge now asks for {found} instead. Only your bridge’s own words are shown above, because a confident explanation of the wrong question is worse than none. This is a defect in Twalk — please report it with the step name below.
networks.step.noExplanationTitle: Twalk has no instructions for this step
networks.step.noExplanationBody: This step hands a credential to your Twalk server, and only your bridge’s own words are shown above — they may not be enough to tell you what you are handing over. Please report it with the step name below.
networks.refused.title: The network would not accept that
networks.refused.body: This is the network refusing what was sent, not a problem with your Twalk server. The network ends the login when it refuses an answer, so there is nothing to correct here: start a new login. If a code was sent to you, you will need a fresh one.
networks.unknownStep.title: This login asks for something this version cannot draw
networks.unknownStep.body: Your Twalk server knows a kind of login step (“{type}”) that this app does not. That happens when the two halves of a deployment are not the same version: the server was updated and this app was not. Reload this page to pick up the current app, or finish this login in the network’s own app.
networks.emoji.body: Your phone is showing an emoji. Check that it is this one, then confirm the pairing on the phone.
networks.emoji.alt: The pairing emoji is {emoji}. Check that your phone shows the same one, then confirm on the phone.
networks.emoji.waiting: Waiting for you to confirm on your phone…
manage.title: Your {network} link
manage.caption: The account this Twalk server is linked to, and what you can do with it.
manage.account.label: Linked account
manage.since.label: Connected since
manage.since.unknown: The bridge has not said since when.
manage.state.label: State
manage.state.connected: This link is working. Messages from this network are reaching your Twalk server.
manage.state.starting: The bridge is bringing this link back up. Nothing to do; it should settle in a moment.
manage.state.degraded: The bridge lost its connection to the network and is reconnecting by itself. Nothing to do.
manage.state.sessionExpired: The network no longer accepts this session — usually because it was removed from your phone's list of linked devices. Re-link to fix it.
manage.state.disconnected: The bridge is not connected to the network with this account.
manage.state.unknown: Your Twalk server could not reach the bridge, so the state of this link is unknown.
manage.relink.hint: Re-linking repairs this session in place. It does not create a second linked device on the network.
manage.disconnect.confirm.title: Disconnect {network} from Twalk?
manage.disconnect.confirm.stops: Your Twalk server stops seeing this network's messages. The Sensor will receive nothing more from it, so your assistant will not read anything new from it either.
manage.disconnect.confirm.keeps: The rooms already created for these conversations stay exactly where they are, with everything already in them. Nothing is deleted, here or on the network.
manage.disconnect.confirm.reversible: You can connect this network again whenever you like — you will scan a code again.
manage.disconnect.failed: The link could not be disconnected. Your Twalk server could not reach the bridge, or the bridge refused. Try again.
manage.disconnected.title: Disconnected
manage.disconnected.body: This network is no longer linked to your Twalk server. The rooms it created are untouched.
manage.noLink.title: Nothing is linked yet
manage.noLink.body: The bridge for this network holds no account. Connect one to start receiving its messages.
manage.unknown.title: This link cannot be checked right now
manage.unknown.body: Your Twalk server could not reach the bridge for this network, so it cannot say whether the account is still linked. That is not the same as being disconnected — check that the bridge is running, then try again.
qr.whatsapp.title: Connect WhatsApp
qr.whatsapp.caption: Twalk signs in to WhatsApp as one more WhatsApp Web session. Your conversations stay end-to-end encrypted between WhatsApp and Twalk; Twalk only observes them.
qr.whatsapp.disclosure.title: About WhatsApp accounts
qr.whatsapp.disclosure.body: Twalk connects to WhatsApp through the same Web protocol as WhatsApp Web. It works with your personal (free) account and needs no WhatsApp Business account. WhatsApp does not officially support third-party clients: in rare cases, an account using Twalk may be temporarily suspended or banned by WhatsApp. Twalk keeps that risk low by following the Web protocol as strictly as it can, but the risk is not zero. You can dismiss this notice once and it will not come back on this device.
qr.whatsapp.step2: Go to Settings, then Linked devices, then Link a device.
qr.whatsapp.step3: Scan this code with your phone's camera.
qr.whatsapp.alt: Scan this code from WhatsApp, under Settings then Linked devices.
qr.whatsapp.success: WhatsApp is connected. Twalk is now observing your WhatsApp conversations.
qr.whatsapp.trouble1: Your phone has to come online at least once every 12 days for the link to stay active.
qr.whatsapp.trouble2: WhatsApp allows up to 4 linked devices on one account. Remove one in WhatsApp if the code is refused.
qr.whatsapp.trouble3: If the code does not scan, hold the phone steady about 20 cm from the screen, and raise your screen's brightness.
qr.signal.title: Connect Signal
qr.signal.caption: Twalk becomes a linked Signal device on your account, just like Signal Desktop. Your phone stays the primary device and is still what recovers your account.
qr.signal.step2: Go to Settings, then Linked devices.
qr.signal.step3: Tap the plus button (Android) or Link new device (iOS).
qr.signal.note: Signal officially supports linked devices: there is no ban risk. Messages sent before this pairing are not synchronised — Twalk sees new messages only.
qr.signal.alt: Scan this code from Signal, under Settings then Linked devices.
qr.signal.success: Signal is connected. Twalk is now observing your new Signal messages.
qr.signal.trouble1: Your phone must stay online for Signal messages to reach Twalk.
qr.signal.trouble2: If the code is refused, check that Signal on your phone is up to date, then show a new code.
qr.telegram.title: Connect Telegram
qr.telegram.caption: Twalk becomes a session of your Telegram account, like Telegram Desktop. Unlike WhatsApp and Signal, your phone does not have to stay on: a Telegram session lives on its own.
qr.telegram.note: Telegram officially supports several sessions: there is no ban risk. You will see this one under Settings then Devices, and you can revoke it from there at any time, without going through Twalk.
qr.telegram.alt: Scan this code from Telegram, under Settings then Devices.
qr.telegram.success: Telegram is connected. Twalk now observes your new Telegram conversations.
qr.telegram.successNote: Your conversations will not all appear at once: Twalk observes only the ones you choose.
qr.telegram.trouble1: If two-step verification is on for your account, Telegram will ask for your password after the scan. That is your Telegram password, not your Twalk one.
qr.telegram.trouble2: A refused code cannot be corrected: Telegram ends the attempt. Start a new login to get a fresh one.
qr.telegram.trouble3: Telegram caps how many sessions an account may have. If linking fails with no visible reason, remove an old session under Settings then Devices.
matrix.title: Connect your Matrix account
matrix.caption: If you already use Matrix, Twalk can watch over the account you have rather than create a new one. Twalk invites its Sensor into the rooms you choose, and changes nothing about your other Matrix sessions.
matrix.homeserverHint: Your server name — the part after the colon in your Matrix ID — or the full address of its homeserver. Twalk follows the server's own redirection.
matrix.foreign.title: This deployment cannot watch that homeserver
matrix.foreign.body: Your account is on {wanted}, and this Twalk deployment is on {deployment}. In this version Twalk can only watch an account on its own homeserver — so nothing is asked of you here, because signing in would not help.
matrix.foreign.why: Watching a room means the Sensor joining it, and a room hosted elsewhere would have to be reached through Matrix federation, which this deployment does not have. A future version watches your account from a device of your own instead, which needs none of that.
matrix.resolved: That server points to {url}, which is where you will sign in.
matrix.ssoReturn: Your homeserver will be asked to send you back to {origin}. A homeserver that only allows return addresses it knows will refuse this one until its administrator adds it.
signin.title: Sign back in
signin.intro: Your session expired, which is normal: the credential that travels on every request is deliberately short-lived. Signing in again takes a moment and changes nothing about your account.
signin.notRecovery: This is not the recovery key screen. Your encryption keys are untouched — a session expiring and a browser losing its keys are different things.
signin.lostKeys: My keys are gone from this device
signin.noAccountYet: This Twalk deployment has no account yet, so there is nothing to sign in to. Set it up first.
signin.error.ssoLost: This sign-in could not be completed, because the browser no longer knows which homeserver it started at. Nothing was sent anywhere. Start again from this screen.
signin.error.ssoNeedsStorage: This browser will not let the sign-in remember where it started, so single sign-on cannot finish here. Use a password, or allow site data for this address.
signin.error.notTheOwner: This account is not the one this Twalk deployment serves.
matrix.noFlow: This homeserver offers no sign-in method the Companion can drive. Sign in from your usual Matrix client, then come back.
matrix.qrLater: Signing in by QR code from another Matrix client (MSC4108) arrives with a later version: it carries your encryption secrets across, and that needs machinery these screens deliberately do not load.
matrix.error.notFound: No Matrix homeserver answered at {domain}. Check the spelling: you can give your server name, like example.com, or the full address of its homeserver.
matrix.error.unreachable: That homeserver could not be reached. Check the address and your internet connection.
matrix.error.ssoLost: This sign-in could not be completed, because the browser no longer knows which homeserver it started at. Nothing was sent anywhere. Enter your homeserver and try again.
matrix.error.ssoNeedsStorage: This browser will not let the sign-in remember where it started, so single sign-on cannot finish here. Use a password, or allow site data for this address.
matrix.error.rejected: The homeserver refused those credentials. Check your username and password.
matrix.error.rateLimited: The homeserver is rate-limiting sign-in attempts. Wait a moment, then try again.
matrix.error.refused: The homeserver refused the sign-in. Try again, and open the diagnostics if it persists.
matrix.error.invite: Your Twalk server could not invite the Sensor. Your Matrix session may have expired — sign in again, then retry.
matrix.error.tokenRejected: Your homeserver would not accept this sign-in, so nothing was invited. Either your Matrix session expired — sign in again above — or this account lives on a homeserver this Twalk deployment cannot reach the Sensor into.
matrix.rooms.intro: These are the rooms {user} has joined. Twalk only learns the ones you tick: the list itself stays in this browser.
matrix.rooms.loading: Reading your rooms from your homeserver…
matrix.rooms.none: This account has joined no rooms yet. Join one from your usual Matrix client, then come back.
matrix.rooms.byAlias: named by its address: this room has no name of its own
matrix.rooms.byMembers: no name: shown by the people in it
matrix.rooms.searchPlaceholder: a name, a person, an address
matrix.rooms.byId: no name and no members to name it after: shown by its identifier
matrix.rooms.invite: {count, plural, =0 {Choose at least one room} one {Invite the Sensor into 1 room} other {Invite the Sensor into # rooms}}
matrix.rooms.onlySelected: Your Matrix password and access token stay in this browser. The only thing sent to your Twalk server is the list of rooms you ticked, and a one-time token that lets it send the invitations.
matrix.done.title: {sensor} has been invited
matrix.done.body: The Sensor joins on its own and starts observing these rooms. Nothing you did not tick is visible to it.
matrix.done.failed: could not be invited — you may not have permission to invite in this room
sms.title: Connect SMS via Google Messages
sms.disclosure.title: This SMS path is a preview
sms.disclosure.body: This is a v0.1 proof of concept. It runs on Google Messages Web, which means your SMS transit through Google's infrastructure and a Google account is required. In v0.2, Twalk replaces it with a first-party Android app that reads SMS straight from your phone with nobody in the middle, and your setup migrates automatically when that ships.
sms.requirement: Twalk uses the Google Messages app on your Android phone to send and receive SMS. You need Google Messages installed and set as the default messaging app on that phone. An iPhone alone cannot use this preview.
sms.ios.title: This preview needs an Android phone
sms.ios.body: SMS through Twalk in v0.1 reads your messages from Google Messages on an Android phone, which iOS does not have. If you own both an iPhone and an Android phone, you can use the Android one as your SMS source. The sovereign path arriving in v0.2 will still need an Android phone.
sms.step1.title: Step 1 — turn on device pairing on your phone
sms.step1.a: Open Google Messages on your Android phone.
sms.step1.b: Tap your profile picture, then Device pairing.
sms.step1.c: Leave that screen open: your phone has to be reachable for the rest of this.
sms.step2.title: Step 2 — hand over your Google Messages session
sms.step2.why: Google switched off the QR sign-in for other Google Messages clients in 2024, so the only way left is to hand over the session cookies your own browser gets when you sign in to Google Messages Web. Twalk cannot read them for you: no web page is allowed to read another site's cookies, and that rule is what protects your other accounts. So you copy them, once.
sms.step2.requirements: Two things to set up first, or the cookies you copy will not work
sms.step2.privateWindow: Use a private window. Signing out of Google in a normal window invalidates the session Twalk is holding, and one day you will sign out without thinking about it. In a private window, close the window instead of signing out and the session stays alive.
sms.step2.dbsc: In Chrome, turn off Device Bound Session Credentials (chrome://flags, search for “device bound”). It ties a Google session to this device's hardware key on purpose, so a copied cookie works nowhere else — including on your Twalk server. It is on by default in recent versions.
sms.step2.a: In a private window, sign in to
sms.step2.b: Pair that browser with your phone by scanning the code Google shows, so the session is a working one.
sms.step2.c: Open the developer tools, go to Application › Storage › Cookies and select https://messages.google.com: that view lists every cookie of the site. Copy the ones listed below into the field.
sms.cookies.where.title: Where the cookies are, and where they are not
sms.cookies.where.application: Application › Storage › Cookies › https://messages.google.com, in the developer tools. That list is complete.
sms.cookies.where.notNetwork: Not “Copy as cURL” on a request in the Network tab: the Messages app talks to instantmessaging-pa.clients6.google.com, and OSID belongs to messages.google.com, so the browser never sends it there — you get six of the seven every time, with nothing to say which is missing or why.
sms.cookies.notThese: Only the cookies listed below are wanted. __Secure-3P*, NID and SIDCC are not among them, and pasting the whole jar would hand over more than the login needs.
sms.cookies.onlyHere: These are your Google account's session cookies. They go into this field, to your own Twalk server, and nowhere else: not into a chat, not into a ticket, not into a support thread — anyone holding them can act as you.
sms.cookies.missingScoped: {scoped} is missing — and not because you copied badly. It belongs to messages.google.com, and a request copied from the Network tab went to Google's API host, which never carries it. Copy the cookies from Application › Storage › Cookies › https://messages.google.com instead.
sms.cookies.whatTheyAre: Together, these are your Google sign-in session: anything holding them can act as you on Google Messages Web for as long as they last. Google documents no lifetime for them, so Twalk promises none — expect to do this again one day. They go to your own Twalk server, which passes them to the bridge and keeps no copy; this browser writes them nowhere. You can end them at any time from your Google account's security settings.
sms.cookies.submit: Send them to my Twalk server
sms.cookies.neverStored: Nothing on this screen is saved in your browser. Close the tab and the paste is gone.
sms.success: SMS is connected through Google Messages.
sms.migration: This network migrates to the sovereign path on its own when v0.2 ships. Nothing to do now.
sms.failed.google: Google refused the session. What it said is quoted below, and Twalk cannot tell more than that from the answer — so it does not guess at a cause. If Google names a two-step challenge, answer it on your phone and copy fresh cookies; if it says something else, redoing the step with the same cookies will not change it, and the answer is what to report.
sms.trouble1: Your Android phone must be online for SMS to reach Twalk. If it is off, your carrier queues the messages until it comes back.
sms.trouble2: If Google asks for a two-factor confirmation while you are signing in, answer it before you copy the cookies: a half-finished sign-in produces cookies that do not work.
sms.trouble3: If SMS stops arriving weeks later, Google most likely ended the session. Come back to this screen and paste a fresh set — that is the price of the preview path, and v0.2 removes it.
error.title: That page does not exist
screen1.error.title: We could not start
screen1.error.gateway: Your Twalk server did not answer. Check your connection, then try again.
screen1.error.homeserver: We could not reach {domain}. Check the address or your internet connection.
screen1.error.notMatrix: {domain} answered, but it is not a Matrix homeserver. Check the address.
screen1.error.notConfigured: This Twalk deployment has no owner configured, so it accepts nobody yet. Ask your administrator.
screen1.signedIn.title: You are signed in
screen1.signedIn.body: This browser already holds a session for {owner}.
screen2.title: Create your account
screen2.subtitle: Twalk will create your account on {domain}.
screen2.username.label: Username
screen2.username.hint: 3 to 30 characters: lowercase letters, digits, underscore, hyphen.
screen2.username.charset: Lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.
screen2.username.taken: This username is already taken on {domain}.
screen2.username.not-the-owner: This deployment was set up for a different username. Ask your administrator which one it expects.
screen2.password.label: Password
screen2.password.hint: At least 12 characters, with a letter and a digit.
screen2.password.needs-letter-and-digit: Add at least one letter and one digit.
screen2.password.refused: Your homeserver refused this password ({errcode}). Try a longer one.
screen2.strength.label: Password strength
screen2.recoveryCard.title: About your recovery key
screen2.recoveryCard.body: Your recovery key unlocks your encrypted conversations if you lose this device. It is generated here, in this page, and Twalk never sees it. Write it down or save it in a password manager: you cannot recover it later.
screen2.step.handover: Connecting Twalk’s Sensor to your account…
screen2.error.closed.title: This Twalk deployment does not allow new accounts
screen2.error.closed.body: Its account was created by its administrator. Ask them for the credentials, or for account creation to be opened.
screen2.error.exists.title: This deployment already has its account
screen2.error.exists.body: One Twalk deployment serves one person, and that account exists. If this is your deployment and your keys are gone from this device, take the recovery path.
screen2.error.recoveryKeyRefused: Twalk refused to send this request because it carried key material. This is a bug in the Companion, not something you did. Please report it.
screen2.error.generic: Your account could not be created. {detail}
key.title: Save your recovery key
key.intro: This is the only time this key is shown. Nothing on your Twalk server, and nothing at Twalk, can show it to you again.
key.label: Your recovery key
key.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the key above and copy it by hand.
key.warning.title: What you lose without it
key.warning.body: This key is what unlocks your encrypted conversations on a new device. Without it, and with this device gone, your message history stays encrypted for ever: nobody — not your Twalk server, not Twalk, not your administrator — can read it back or reset it. Your other devices can no longer be verified either, so Twalk would treat them as strangers.
key.warning.noReset: There is no reset in this version. A lost key cannot be replaced; only a new account can.
key.checkbox: I have saved my recovery key in a safe place
key.backup.on: Your key backup is on: new messages are backed up, encrypted with this key.
key.backup.off: Your key backup could not be started. Your recovery key is still valid; open diagnostics before going further.
pdf.title: Twalk recovery key
pdf.intro: This sheet carries the only copy of your Twalk recovery key. It unlocks your encrypted conversations on a new device.
pdf.warning: Keep this sheet. Without this key, and without the device you created it on, your encrypted messages cannot be read back by anyone, and there is no way to reset it.
pdf.advice1: Keep it somewhere you would keep a passport or a bank card: a safe, a locked drawer, a password manager.
pdf.advice2: Do not photograph it, do not email it, and do not put it in a note on your phone.
pdf.advice3: Anyone who has this key can read your conversation history. Twalk never sees it.
pdf.generated: Generated on {date} by the Twalk Companion.
done.title: Your account is ready
done.body: {id} exists, your cryptographic identity is set up, and your recovery key is saved.
done.next.title: Next: connect a network
done.next.body: Connect WhatsApp, Signal, SMS or an existing Matrix account, then activate your assistant on it. If your Twalk server has no bridge configured, the Matrix card is the one that will work — the others say so on the screen.
handover.ready: Twalk can reach its Sensor with your account’s encryption.
handover.problem.title: Twalk cannot reach its Sensor yet
handover.problem.noSensor: This Twalk server runs no Sensor, so there is nothing to connect your account to. Your administrator sets GATEWAY_SENSOR_USER_ID.
handover.problem.didNotJoin: Twalk’s Sensor was invited and has not accepted. It accepts invitations from the accounts SENSOR_ALLOWED_INVITERS names, and your administrator can check that yours is one of them — and that the Sensor is running.
handover.problem.untracked: Twalk’s Sensor is there and this browser does not yet know its encryption keys, so a message sent to it now would arrive empty. Reloading this page later retries it.
handover.problem.after: Everything else works. What this stops is Twalk replying on your behalf, which nothing does yet in this version.
recover.title: Your keys are not on this device
recover.intro: This is normal, not a failure. Twalk keeps your encryption keys in this browser alone, and a browser can throw them away — iOS deletes them after seven days without opening the app, and clearing your browsing data does it too.
recover.fix: Your recovery key puts them back. Nothing is lost.
recover.domain.label: Your Twalk domain
recover.install: Install Twalk to your home screen to stop iOS from doing it again.
recover.userId.label: Username
recover.userId.hintNoDomain: The username you created on your Twalk deployment.
recover.domain.hint: The address of the Twalk deployment your account is on, with its port if it has one. This browser has not been here before, so it cannot know.
recover.password.label: Password
recover.key.label: Your recovery key
recover.key.not-base58: This key carries a character a recovery key never has. Check for a 0, an O, an I or an l.
recover.key.wrong-length: A recovery key is 12 groups of four characters.
recover.key.not-a-recovery-key: This is a key, but not a Twalk recovery key.
recover.key.parity: There is a typo in this key: two characters do not add up.
recover.error.wrong-recovery-key: This recovery key does not open this account's storage. Check it group by group.
recover.error.no-secret-storage: This account has no recovery storage, so there is nothing a recovery key opens.
recover.error.unreachable: Nothing answered at {url}, so nothing has seen your password or your key yet. Check the address above — a port is easy to leave out — and your connection.
recover.error.failed: The recovery could not be completed. {detail}
recover.done.title: This device is back
recover.done.body: Your keys are on this device again and it is verified. Your encrypted conversations open as before.
recover.done.unverified: Your keys came back, but this device could not be verified. Open diagnostics before going further.
recover.done.backup: Your key backup is connected again.
tabs.title: Twalk is open in another tab
tabs.body: Twalk keeps your encryption keys in one place, and two tabs writing to it at once would damage them. Go back to the other tab, or take over here.
tabs.unanswered.title: The other tab is not answering
tabs.unanswered.body: Twalk asked the other tab to let go and heard nothing back for {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}. That tab is still open: your browser puts tabs to sleep when it thinks you have forgotten them, and a sleeping tab keeps its hold on your keys without being able to answer.
tabs.unanswered.remedy: Find the other Twalk tab and close it. Switching to it is enough to wake it, and this button then works. If you cannot find it, restarting your browser releases the hold.
persona.assistant.name: Assistant
persona.assistant.description: Your assistant reads the messages arriving on the networks you connected, and suggests replies for you to review. It never sends anything without your approval.
persona.ability.read.label: Read incoming messages
persona.ability.read.detail: On the networks you choose below, and on no others.
persona.ability.read.locked: Always on: an assistant that reads nothing has nothing to suggest.
persona.ability.suggest.label: Suggest replies for your review
persona.ability.suggest.detail: A suggestion waits for you. Nothing leaves your deployment until you approve it.
persona.ability.suggest.locked: Always on: reading and suggesting are one decision in this version — the assistant is active, or it is paused.
persona.title: Activate your first agent
persona.scope.title: What it may read
persona.scope.intro: The assistant is activated on exactly the networks you tick here. Connecting another network later leaves it inactive there until you say otherwise.
persona.scope.matrixHint: Your Twalk deployment keeps no record of the rooms you invited the Sensor into — the access token that did it was forgotten as soon as the invitation was sent. Tick this if you connected your existing Matrix account.
persona.scope.none: No network is connected yet. Connect one first, and the assistant will have something to read.
persona.scope.unknown: Twalk could not read which networks this deployment has connected, so this screen cannot say what the assistant would be allowed to read. Try again rather than activating it blind.
persona.consent.title: Who the assistant may read, by default
persona.consent.body: Every contact starts at pending. The assistant reads nothing from someone until you decide about them, and there is no rule that grants anyone automatically — this version imports no address book.
persona.removed.title: Two settings the wireframe had, and this screen does not
persona.removed.autoSend: Auto-sending approved replies. It is the one thing in Twalk that would let an agent send without you, so it is not a toggle in an onboarding flow.
persona.removed.hours: Active hours. A time window is a rule to be enforced and audited at runtime; a cosmetic control here would suggest a protection that does not exist.
persona.runtime.title: What happens after you activate it
persona.runtime.body: The decision is recorded and published on your bus, where the agent runtime reads it: the assistant starts from the networks you chose, and from nothing else.
persona.pause.meaning: Pausing an assistant means it receives nothing. It keeps running and stays supervised — it is starved, not stopped.
persona.activated.title: Your assistant is now watching {networks}.
persona.activated.body: It is activated on those networks and on no others.
persona.error.noNetworks: Tick at least one network: an assistant with no perimeter is not a decision the deployment can record.
persona.error.refused: Your deployment refused the decision ({error}). Nothing was recorded.
persona.error.unreachable: Your deployment could not be reached. Nothing was recorded — try again.
dashboard.title: Your Twalk
dashboard.unreachable: Your deployment could not be reached. What you see below is the last answer it gave.
dashboard.health.setupDetail: Connect a network and activate your assistant to finish setting Twalk up.
dashboard.banner.expired.title: Your {network} session expired.
dashboard.banner.expired.body: Reconnect to keep receiving messages from it.
dashboard.chip.pending: {count, plural, one {# consent decision waiting for you} other {# consent decisions waiting for you}}
dashboard.bridges.title: Networks
dashboard.bridges.none: No bridge is configured on this deployment.
dashboard.bridges.note: These read what each bridge says about the account linked to it. The time of the last message is not reported by this deployment yet.
dashboard.personas.title: Agents
dashboard.persona.pausedMeaning: A paused agent receives nothing. It keeps running and stays supervised — it is starved, not stopped.
dashboard.persona.failed: The decision was refused ({error}). Nothing changed.
runtime.present: Your agent runtime is running here and hosting {count, plural, one {one assistant} other {# assistants}}. An active assistant reads what you allowed and proposes replies for you to approve.
runtime.gone: An agent runtime ran here and is not running now. An active assistant produces nothing until it is back; your decisions are recorded and honoured the moment it returns.
runtime.never: No agent runtime has hosted an assistant here yet, so an active assistant produces nothing today. Your decision is recorded and published, and the runtime honours it from the day it starts.
runtime.noBus: This server has no event bus configured, so no agent runtime can run against it: an assistant here can read nothing and propose nothing.
runtime.unknown: Whether an agent runtime is running could not be read from your server just now.
dashboard.messages.title: Messages carried
dashboard.feed.title: Recent activity
dashboard.feed.privacy: Operational events only: bridges, consent and agents, plus a count. Twalk does not keep a list of who writes to you, so this screen cannot show one.
dashboard.feed.move.followed: A conversation you observe moved to a new room of {members} people; your decision followed it
dashboard.feed.move.returned: A conversation you observe moved to a new room of {members} people — at or above {threshold}, it is back in the chooser for you to decide again
dashboard.devices.title: Your devices
dashboard.devices.confirmCurrent: This is the device you are using. Revoking it signs you out here. Continue?
dashboard.devices.failed: That device could not be revoked ({error}).
dashboard.devices.none: No device has signed in yet.
dashboard.messagr.title: Pair with Messagr
dashboard.messagr.body: Messagr is LINAGORA's messaging interface. Pairing the Companion with it is not available in this version.
done.next.after: After that: activate your assistant on the networks you connected, and land on your dashboard.
dashboard.chip.inbox: They are people who have written to you and whom you have never decided about. Deciding is one person at a time.
approvals.title: Replies waiting for you
approvals.step: Your assistant proposes; you decide. Nothing is sent until you say so.
approvals.deliberate: There is no “approve everything” here, and nothing is ticked for you: each reply is approved on its own, by pressing its own button.
approvals.empty.title: Nothing is waiting
approvals.empty.body: No persona has proposed a reply in the stretch of the event stream this server reads.
approvals.empty.noRuntime: No agent runtime is running against this deployment right now, so nothing can be proposed: there is nothing wrong here, and there is nothing to approve.
approvals.empty.notActivated: Your assistant is not activated on any network, so it proposes nothing. Activate it from the dashboard when you want it to.
approvals.empty.nothingProposed: Your assistant is active and has proposed nothing in this stretch of the stream: no message it may read has arrived. There is nothing wrong, and there is nothing to approve.
approvals.empty.unknown: Whether your assistant is active, or whether an agent runtime is running, could not be read just now — so this screen cannot say why the list is empty.
approvals.row.expiresNever: No expiry: this one can be approved at any later date.
approvals.trigger.message: A reply to a message on {network}
approvals.trigger.other: A reply to a {network} event of type {type}
approvals.whoIsIt.title: This screen cannot tell you who it is to
approvals.whoIsIt.body: Your server lists what your assistant wrote, and identifies the message it answers by its reference alone — never by the sender, never by a quote of what they said. Reading their message to label this row would copy a contact’s words somewhere they had not travelled before. Whether that trade is the right one is an open question on the project, and this is what the answer costs today.
approvals.expired.reason: This suggestion went stale before you got to it. Nothing keeps a copy of it, so it cannot be approved late — it is shown rather than hidden so you know what became of it. Ask your assistant for a new one by writing to the person again.
approvals.stale: This one has gone stale while this screen was open. Approving it will be refused; refresh to see where it stands.
approvals.editing.label: The reply that will be sent
approvals.editing.hint: Nothing is sent by typing here, and no key sends it. Press “Approve and send” when the text says what you mean.
approvals.editing.empty: An empty reply would send an empty message. Write something, or keep what was proposed.
approvals.dismiss.meaning: Refusing hides this reply on this browser. Your assistant is not told, nothing is recorded on your server, and the suggestion goes stale on its own.
approvals.approvedText.label: What you sent
approvals.sent.title: Published
approvals.sent.body: Approved as {owner} and published on your event stream at position {sequence}. That is all your server can say by itself: your Sensor posts it into the conversation from there, then says who received it.
approvals.sent.unedited: Published as your assistant wrote it.
approvals.delivery.canReach: Your account is in this conversation: once approved, the reply is relayed to the contact by the network, as if you had written it.
approvals.delivery.cannotReach: This reply cannot reach the contact. Your account is not in this conversation ({detail}), and a bridge relays only what your own account sends: approving would publish it on your stream, and nobody would receive it. What changes this is the device that acts in your name (#123) — it has to have joined the conversation. This is not a fault in your setup.
approvals.delivery.unknown: Twalk cannot tell in advance whether it will reach the contact ({detail}). Your Sensor will say once the reply is posted.
approvals.delivery.detail.owner_invited: your account was invited and none of your devices accepted
approvals.delivery.detail.owner_absent: your account is not in it and was not invited
approvals.delivery.detail.not_a_known_po: none of your bridges knows this conversation — a Matrix conversation, most likely
approvals.delivery.detail.portal_unreada: one of your bridges could not be asked
approvals.delivery.detail.no_portal_regi: your server has no register of conversations
approvals.delivery.detail.no_owner_confi: your server does not know your account
approvals.delivery.detail.trigger_out_of: the message it answers lies beyond the stretch of the stream your server reads
approvals.delivery.detail.lookup_failed: the event stream did not answer
approvals.posted.contact: Delivered: your Sensor posted it as {postedAs} into the conversation, and the network relayed it to the contact.
approvals.posted.nobody: Nobody received it: your Sensor posted it as {postedAs}, an account the conversation's bridge ignores because it is not yours (#123). It exists in a room the contact cannot see.
approvals.posted.pending: Your Sensor has not posted it yet — or did so beyond the stretch of the stream your server reads.
approvals.lost.title: This reply did not go out
approvals.lost.body: Your server recorded your approval and the event stream never acknowledged the reply, so it was never posted. Approving again republishes the very same reply — it cannot be sent twice, whatever happens.
approvals.notice.window: Your server reads back only a stretch of the event stream, and it did not reach the beginning. Suggestions older than that stretch exist and are not listed here.
approvals.notice.truncated: More replies were found than are shown. The rest are older; approve or refuse these and refresh.
approvals.notice.unreadable: {count, plural, one {# reply in this stretch could not be read by your server, and is not listed} other {# replies in this stretch could not be read by your server, and are not listed}}: it carries something this version does not understand.
approvals.notice.dismissed: {count, plural, one {# reply is hidden because you refused it here} other {# replies are hidden because you refused them here}}.
approvals.refusal.malformed_request: Your server did not accept the request this screen made. That is a defect in the Companion rather than anything you did.
approvals.refusal.approval_is_not_a_batc: Your server was asked to approve more than one reply at once, and refused. An approval is one reply, deliberately — that refusal is the product working, and this screen should not have asked.
approvals.refusal.unknown_value: The reply’s format is not one your server knows.
approvals.refusal.approved_by_is_not_the: Your server refuses to record an approval under a name that is not its owner’s. Nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.unauthenticated: Your server answered, and would not accept this session. Nothing is wrong with your deployment.
approvals.refusal.suggestion_not_found: This suggestion is no longer on your event stream. Your server read the whole of what it keeps and did not find it.
approvals.refusal.trigger_not_found: The message this reply answers is no longer on your event stream, so there is no conversation to send it to. Nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.suggestion_out_of_reac: This suggestion is older than the stretch of the event stream your server reads back. It may still be there; your server stopped looking before it got that far — and a suggestion that old has gone stale in any case.
approvals.refusal.trigger_out_of_reach: The message this reply answers is older than the stretch your server reads back, so it could not be found and nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.suggestion_expired: This suggestion went stale before you approved it. Nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.consent_revoked: You have revoked your consent for this contact since your assistant wrote this reply, so nothing was sent. Consent is checked at the moment you approve, never when the reply was drafted.
approvals.refusal.consent_pending: You have not decided about this contact, so nothing was sent. Consent is checked at the moment you approve.
approvals.refusal.suggestion_was_never_c: The message this answers was observed without your consent, so this reply should never have been drafted and will not be sent.
approvals.refusal.already_approved: You have already approved this reply. It was not sent a second time — refresh to see where the first one landed.
approvals.refusal.trigger_has_no_room: The message this reply answers does not name a conversation, so there is nowhere to send it.
approvals.refusal.suggestion_unreadable: This suggestion carries something your server’s version does not understand, so it will not act on it. It was found, and not misread.
approvals.refusal.bus_unreachable: Your server could not reach its event stream, so nothing was read and nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.store_unavailable: Your server could not read its own records, so it would not say anything half-known. Nothing was sent.
approvals.refusal.approval_published_but: Your reply was sent. Your server could not write down that it had, so it will not appear as approved until you approve it once more — which republishes the very same reply and cannot send it twice.
approvals.refusal.approvals_not_configur: This deployment approves nothing: it has no event stream configured, so there is nothing to read a suggestion from and nothing to publish a reply on.
approvals.refusal.suggestions_not_config: This deployment reads no suggestions: it has no event stream configured. That is not the same as “nobody has proposed anything” — your server is not watching.
approvals.refusal.unknown: Your server refused, with a reason this version of the Companion does not know ({error}). Nothing was sent.
approvals.remedy.reload: Refresh this screen to see where things stand.
approvals.remedy.signIn: Sign in again to carry on.
approvals.remedy.diagnostics: Open the diagnostics and report this, with the code above.
approvals.remedy.none: There is nothing to do here, and nothing was half-done.
dashboard.chip.suggestions: {count, plural, one {# reply is waiting for your approval} other {# replies are waiting for your approval}}
dashboard.chip.suggestionsAtLeast: At least this many: your server read back only part of the event stream.
dashboard.chip.suggestionsPrivate: What your assistant wrote is not shown here. This screen gets unlocked on a train.
consent.title: Your decisions about your contacts
consent.step: You decide, one person at a time, whose messages Twalk may process.
consent.intro.title: What this screen decides
consent.intro.body: Your assistant may only read the messages of a contact you have granted. This is where you grant one, revoke one, or say “not yet”.
consent.intro.notTheirs: This is your decision, not theirs. Your contacts are neither asked nor told, and “granted” records that you decided — never that anybody agreed.
consent.legend.title: The three answers, and what each one does
consent.legend.granted: Your assistant may read what this person writes, and may propose replies to them.
consent.legend.pending: The message still arrives on your server, in full, and your assistant is expected to leave it alone. This answer hides nothing from your own server.
consent.legend.revoked: The message still arrives, as a record that it did, but without what was written: no text, no quoted message, no attachment. This is the only answer that withholds content.
consent.legend.neverDecided: A contact you have never decided about is its own thing, and not the same as one you answered “not yet” about. It is where everybody starts, and it will be most of this list.
consent.legend.notRetroactive: None of this reaches the past. The answer is stamped on each message as it arrives, so a decision you take now applies to what comes next and changes nothing already on your server. If you grant somebody and nothing seems to happen, wait for their next message: that is how it is meant to work.
consent.count.awaiting: {count, plural, =0 {nobody is waiting for a first answer} one {1 person is waiting for a first answer} other {# people are waiting for a first answer}}
consent.count.gateway: Your server counts {count, plural, one {# contact} other {# contacts}} waiting for a first answer. Where that differs from the number above, some of them wrote on a network this version of the app does not know about.
consent.empty.title: Nobody to decide about
consent.empty.body: Nobody has written yet, and nobody has been decided about. Connect a network and this list fills itself as people write to you.
consent.search.label: Search your contacts
consent.search.placeholder: A name, a number, a Matrix ID
consent.bulk.title: Answer for everyone shown
consent.bulk.scope: This acts on the {shown, plural, one {# contact} other {# contacts}} the search is showing right now, and on nobody else. Narrow the search first if that is not the group you mean.
consent.bulk.grant: {count, plural, one {Grant the one shown} other {Grant all # shown}}
consent.bulk.revoke: {count, plural, one {Revoke the one shown} other {Revoke all # shown}}
consent.bulk.confirmGrant: {count, plural, one {Grant # contact?} other {Grant # contacts?}} Your assistant will be able to read everything they write from now on.
consent.bulk.confirmRevoke: {count, plural, one {Revoke # contact?} other {Revoke # contacts?}} What they write from now on arrives without its content.
consent.bulk.done: {count, plural, one {# decision recorded} other {# decisions recorded}}: {state}.
consent.bulk.partial: Whatever was recorded before this failure is recorded. Refresh to see what.
consent.row.byId: Your server no longer holds a name for this person, so this is the identity their network gave them.
consent.row.neverDecided: Nobody has decided about this person yet.
consent.row.fromNetwork: This comes from your answer for {network} as a whole, which is “{state}”. Answering for this person below overrides it.
consent.row.overrides: Your answer for {network} as a whole is “{state}”, and this person’s own answer wins over it.
consent.row.isOwner: This is you, and you are not one of your own contacts. There is nothing to decide here — see the note above.
consent.action.undecideMeaning: “Not yet” is an answer, not an undo: it is recorded like the other two, and this person stops being counted as waiting for a first one. Nothing in this version can unsay a decision — the record only ever grows.
consent.decided.notRetroactive: It applies to their next message, not to the ones already on your server.
consent.waiting.missing: Everything you have already decided is below and is up to date. What is missing is the people who have written to you and whom you have never decided about: that list comes from a different read, and it is the one that failed.
consent.names.unreadable: Your server could not read back what these contacts are called, so they are shown by the identity their network gave them. The list itself is complete: names are looked up separately and never stored.
consent.owner.title: You are listed as one of your own contacts
consent.owner.body: {id} is this deployment’s own account, and it should never appear here: you are not somebody you decide about. It is a record left over from before your server learned to recognise you, and a known defect rather than something you did.
consent.owner.remedy: It is shown rather than hidden so that you know it is there, and no decision is offered on it: answering it would silence your own messages for anything reading that record. Nothing on this screen can remove it.
consent.networks.note: Answering for a whole network at once decides for everybody on it, including people who have not written yet. That is deliberately not offered here: this screen decides about people one at a time.
consent.refusal.malformed_request: Your server refused this decision as malformed. This app built the request, so this is a defect in the app rather than anything you did.
consent.refusal.unknown_value: Your server did not recognise a value this app sent — a network, or an answer. This app built the request, so this is a defect in the app.
consent.refusal.unsupported_subject_type: Your server does not accept a decision about this kind of subject. This app built the request, so this is a defect in the app.
consent.refusal.scope_contradicts_subjec: Your server refused the perimeter this app asked for. This app built the request, so this is a defect in the app.
consent.refusal.subject_is_the_owner: That identity is your own. You are never one of your own contacts, so there is nothing to decide about yourself — and nothing was recorded.
consent.refusal.unauthenticated: Your server answered, and would not accept this session. Nothing is wrong with your deployment.
consent.refusal.store_unavailable: Your server could not read or write its record of decisions. Nothing was recorded and nothing was announced — which is why you are being shown a failure instead of being told it worked.
consent.refusal.consent_not_configured: This deployment records no decisions at all: it has no event bus, so it refuses to record one it could not announce. Your session and the rest of the app are unaffected.
consent.refusal.contacts_not_configured: This deployment is not watching incoming messages, so it has no list of people waiting for an answer. That is not the same statement as nobody having written to you.
consent.refusal.bus_unreachable: Your server could not read back what these contacts are called. Only the names are affected; the list is complete.
consent.refusal.unknown: Your server refused this with a reason this version of the app has no words for. Your server’s own logs name it.
consent.remedy.reload: Refresh this screen: what it is showing is out of date.
consent.remedy.signIn: Sign in again to carry on.
consent.remedy.diagnostics: Open the diagnostics and report what it says: this should not happen.
consent.remedy.none: There is nothing to do from here.
session.expired.title: Your session has expired
session.expired.body: Twalk signs each browser in for a short while at a time, and this one's turn is over. Sign in again to carry on.
session.expired.bodyFor: Twalk signs each browser in for a short while at a time, and this one's turn is over. Sign in again as {owner} to carry on.
session.expired.stay: Nothing is wrong with your Twalk server and nothing was lost. You will come straight back to this screen, and the networks you have connected are still connected.
conversations.title: Which conversations Twalk watches
conversations.caption: Nothing is watched until you say so. Choose one conversation at a time — and read the number beside it before you do.
conversations.summary: Twalk is reading {observing} of your {total, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}.
conversations.strangers: The people in these conversations have not been told about Twalk. Watching one means their messages reach your Twalk server, and what happens to them afterwards is the consent you set per person.
conversations.loading: Asking your Twalk server which conversations your networks have built…
conversations.none: Your networks have not built any conversation yet. They are built one at a time, as a conversation becomes active — so come back after somebody writes to you, and they will be here.
conversations.notConfigured.title: This screen could not read your conversations
conversations.notConfigured.body: Your Twalk server has no way to look at your networks' conversations yet. It needs each bridge's own credentials, which is a change to your deployment's configuration and not something this screen can do.
conversations.search.label: Search your conversations
conversations.members: {count, plural, =0 {nobody else} one {# person} other {# people}}
conversations.moved: moved here from an earlier room
conversations.movedWhy: You were observing this conversation, and its room was replaced by a new one that Twalk is not in. The new room holds more people than the threshold you acknowledged, so the decision is yours again: tick it to observe it where it now lives.
conversations.crowdMoved: a conversation you were observing, which moved to a larger room — this is the size it has now
conversations.invitedWhy: Twalk was asked into this conversation and has not come in. That is a setting on your Twalk server: the part that reads your messages has not been told to accept invitations from this network's bridge.
conversations.kind.oneToOne.why: A conversation with one other person. The network itself says so, by the address it gives the conversation.
conversations.kind.group.why: A group, again by the network's own address for it. Watching one means watching everybody who writes in it.
conversations.kind.community.why: A community is several groups at once: the community itself, its announcements, and its subgroups. The number beside each one is how many people it covers.
conversations.kind.community.caveat: Your network never tells Twalk which groups belong to the same community, so these are grouped because their names say they belong together. Twalk will not guess which one is the community and which is its announcements — the count and the address under each name are what tell them apart.
conversations.kind.broadcast.why: A status broadcast or a channel: messages sent to many people rather than a conversation with them.
conversations.kind.unstated.why: The network did not say whether these are one person or a group, and Twalk will not guess from how many people are in them. Read the name and the count before choosing.
conversations.family.head: {conversations, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}, {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} in all
conversations.family.select: Watch all {count} — that is {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}
conversations.consequence.none: Nothing would change. Tick a conversation to start watching it, or untick one to stop.
conversations.consequence.adding: You are about to let Twalk read {conversations, plural, one {# new conversation} other {# new conversations}}: {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}.
conversations.consequence.largest: The largest is {name}, with {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} in it.
conversations.consequence.stopping: And to stop watching {count, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}.
conversations.acknowledge.title: This covers {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}
conversations.acknowledge.body: None of them has been told about Twalk. Their messages will reach your Twalk server for as long as you watch these conversations, and you can stop at any time from this screen.
conversations.acknowledge.label: I have read this, and I am choosing to watch {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}.
conversations.apply.start: Watch {count, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}
conversations.apply.stop: Stop watching {count, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}
conversations.apply.both: Watch {starting, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}}, stop watching {stopping}
conversations.outcome.invited: Twalk was asked in, and joins on its own.
conversations.outcome.notObserved: Was not watched to begin with.
conversations.outcome.unknownPortal: Your Twalk server no longer holds this conversation. Reload the screen.
conversations.outcome.failed: This one did not work ({reason}). The others were unaffected.
conversations.bridgeUnreadable: None of {bridge}'s conversations are in this list: your Twalk server could not read them.
conversations.bridgeAskedNothing: {bridge} answered, and the account your Twalk server asked as ({account}) is in no conversation at all. Either this network has not built one yet, or your server is asking as the wrong account — the second is a configuration problem and the logs name the setting.
api.trouble.unreachable: Your Twalk server could not be reached: nothing answered at all. Check that it is running, and check your connection.
api.trouble.sessionRefused: Your Twalk server answered, and would not accept this session. Sign in again to carry on — nothing else is wrong.
api.trouble.refused: Your Twalk server answered, but could not do this. Try again, and open the diagnostics if it persists.
